exposure: Presence of obstetric nurse at delivery time
outcome: Coexistence and prevalence of obstetric interventions (e.g., diet, freedom to move, partogram use, non-pharmacological pain relief, enema, perineal shaving, lying patients down for delivery, Kristeller maneuver, amniotomy, oxytocin infusion, analgesia, episiotomy)
Obstetric care profiles (Profile 1: evidence-based care; Profile 2: non-evidence-based care)
cohort: The study included parturient women from maternity hospitals in Belo Horizonte City, Brazil, whose data derived from the 'Nascer em Belo Horizonte: Inquerito sobre o Parto e Nascimento' (Born in Belo Horizonte: Survey on Childbirth and Birth) study.
finding: The study identified two antagonistic obstetric profiles, one reflecting evidence-based care and another reflecting non-evidence-based care, with the presence of obstetric nurses and public institution childbirth reducing the likelihood of belonging to the non-evidence-based care profile.
cross-section timing: Data derived from the 'Nascer em Belo Horizonte: Inquerito sobre o Parto e Nascimento' (Born in Belo Horizonte: Survey on Childbirth and Birth) study, but specific timing of data collection within that study is not detailed.
